headline: POW Terms Leave Abu Dhabi Short of a Peace Settlement
deck: Kushner said Russia and Ukraine agreed final exchange terms, but territorial differences remain outside the prisoner deal.
body: Jared Kushner, the U.S. presidential envoy, said Russia and Ukraine had agreed final terms for a prisoner-of-war exchange after talks in Moscow. One day earlier, this paper reported that the sides had agreed to an exchange without disclosing its size or timing. [E1] [E7]

After the Abu Dhabi talks, Kushner had called the planned deal the war’s biggest humanitarian release and said its numbers still had to be finalized. Vladimir Medinsky, head of the Russian delegation, and Rustem Umerov, who led Kyiv’s contingent, also confirmed a planned exchange, although Medinsky described the agreement as “in principle.” [E2] [E3]

Reuters reported that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to include European nations in the next round of talks. Kyiv and Moscow nonetheless said major differences remained, particularly over territory; Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the Ukrainian leader, said Ukraine would not cede occupied territory in exchange for peace. Russia holds one-fifth of Ukraine, according to the Jerusalem Post. [E5] [E6] [E4]

The exchange is a concrete humanitarian result because final terms concern a defined release, which Kushner described as a humanitarian one, and both delegations have confirmed the planned action. [E1] [E2] [E3] That agreement can address prisoners’ return without resolving the territorial question that remains attached to peace terms. [E6] [E4]

**The desk's reading.** The stronger reading is that Abu Dhabi has produced a narrow humanitarian result: an exchange whose terms have moved beyond the earlier announcement. The best competing reading is that the same agreement, alongside a broader next round, puts a settlement within reach. But the recorded territorial divide supplies the separate condition a settlement still has to cross. [E5] [E6] [E4]

**The next test.** At the next round, the Russian and Ukrainian delegations should either jointly publish matching territorial terms or their leaders should endorse the same territorial framework. Actual prisoner releases without that shared territorial position would support the narrow humanitarian reading; matching territorial terms would support the settlement-within-reach reading.

The Ukrainian leader gave a muted welcome to the outcome of the talks, saying a proposed prisoner exchange was a positive step. But he said Ukraine will not give in to demands that it cede its territory that has been occupied by Russia in exchange for peace.
